formCues: Punch bar overhead as you drop under it
Lock out arms with feet re-set
setup: Stand with a loaded barbell racked across the front shoulders in a shoulder-width stance.
commonMistakes: Pressing out with arms before leg drive
Leaning back during the dip
Not re-bending knees to catch overhead

formCues: Keep body in a straight line
Lower chest to just above floor
setup: Start in a plank position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width under the shoulders.
commonMistakes: Letting hips sag
Flaring elbows out too wide
Partial range of motion

formCues: At the top, protract shoulder blades further
setup: Start in a standard push-up plank position with hands under shoulders.
commonMistakes: Skipping the protraction phase
Shrugging shoulders instead of protracting
Losing plank alignment

setup: Start on hands and knees with one hand lightly behind the head.
commonMistakes: Rotating through the lower back or hips
Moving too fast
Limited range from tight thoracic spine

formCues: Set pins just below knee height
Keep back flat and chest up
setup: Set a barbell on safety pins in a squat rack at or just below knee level and grip it shoulder-width.
commonMistakes: Setting pins too low, turning it into a deadlift
Rounding the lower back
Hyperextending at lockout

formCues: Keep lower back flat on floor
Flex ankle to protect the knee
Breathe and relax into the stretch
setup: Lie on your back, cross one ankle over the opposite knee, and clasp hands behind the bottom thigh.
commonMistakes: Pulling the knee instead of the thigh
Lifting hips off the floor
Forcing the stretch with tension

formCues: Keep spine neutral on the mat
Flex foot to protect knee joint
setup: Lie on your back and cross one ankle over the opposite knee, feet flexed.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back off the mat
Overstretching the knee joint
Rushing instead of holding steadily

formCues: Adjust seat so knee has slight bend at extension
setup: Sit back in the reclined seat with feet strapped into the pedals and hands resting on the side or console.
commonMistakes: Seat too far forward causing knee strain
Locking knees at full extension
Slouching against the backrest

setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms back, ready to jump forward repeatedly.
commonMistakes: Landing with stiff, locked knees
Pausing too long between jumps
Losing forward momentum on reset

setup: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with feet hip-width apart, holding the ends at your sides.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso for momentum
Letting elbows drift forward
Releasing tension too fast on the way down

setup: Stand on a resistance band with a neutral grip on each handle, arms at your sides.
commonMistakes: Using shoulder momentum to curl
Elbows drifting away from torso
Rotating wrists into a standard curl

setup: Stand on the band with feet shoulder-width apart, holding handles at shoulder height.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back excessively
Pressing the band forward instead of up
Shrugging shoulders during the press

formCues: Keep upper arm parallel to torso
setup: Anchor the band under one foot, hinge forward, and hold the handle with elbow bent at your side.
commonMistakes: Swinging the upper arm during extension
Not fully hinging at the hips
Using momentum instead of triceps

setup: Anchor a band overhead and grip it with both hands, elbows bent at your sides.
commonMistakes: Letting elbows flare outward
Using body weight instead of triceps to push
Cutting the range of motion short

formCues: Curl hips off the floor using abs
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent at 90 degrees and hands flat by your sides.
commonMistakes: Using momentum by swinging the legs
Pulling with the hip flexors instead of abs
Lifting the head and neck to assist

formCues: Grip bar with palms facing you
setup: Lie on a bench and grip the barbell with an underhand (supinated) grip slightly outside shoulder width.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows too wide
Using too heavy a load without wrist strength
Bouncing the bar off the chest

setup: Stand facing a high cable pulley and grip the attachment underhand with elbows bent at your sides.
commonMistakes: Letting elbows drift away from the body
Using body lean instead of triceps
Not fully extending the arms

setup: Sit at a lat pulldown machine and grip the bar underhand at shoulder width, thighs secured under the pad.
commonMistakes: Leaning back excessively to use momentum
Pulling the bar behind the neck
Not achieving full stretch at the top

formCues: Avoid arching the lower back excessively
setup: Lie face down on the reverse hyper machine with hips at the edge of the pad and ankles secured on the roller.
commonMistakes: Using momentum instead of controlled glute contraction
Hyperextending the lumbar spine
Swinging legs too high

formCues: Push hips up to form a straight line
Fingers point toward feet or away
setup: Sit with legs extended, hands placed behind hips, then lift hips into a straight bridge line.
commonMistakes: Letting hips sag toward the floor
Shrugging shoulders up toward ears
Overextending the neck

formCues: Explode up and switch legs mid-air
Land softly in the opposite lunge
setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, ready to step back into an explosive lunge.
commonMistakes: Landing with a stiff front knee
Letting the knee cave inward
Losing balance on the switch

formCues: Reach back hand toward back leg
setup: From a warrior II stance, drop the back hand to the back leg and reach the front arm overhead.
commonMistakes: Letting the front knee collapse inward
Losing the bend in the front leg
Collapsing the side body instead of lengthening

formCues: Sit hips back like into a chair
setup: Stand with feet together, bend knees into a chair pose, then bring hands together at the chest.
commonMistakes: Letting knees splay apart during the twist
Rotating from the lower back instead of the torso
Losing the squat depth while twisting

formCues: Hinge forward with a flat back
Rotate torso and reach top arm up
setup: From a forward fold, shift weight to one leg, lift the back leg, and place the opposite hand on the floor.
commonMistakes: Letting hips open before establishing balance
Rounding the back during the hinge
Wobbling from a narrow base of support

formCues: Square hips toward the front foot
Hinge from the hips, not the waist
Rotate torso and reach opposite hand to shin or floor
setup: Stand in a lunge-length stance with front foot forward, hips squared toward that foot.
commonMistakes: Rounding the spine instead of hinging
Letting the back hip open up
Forcing the hand to the floor and losing hip square

formCues: Arms straight, rings at hip level
Engage lats and shoulders to resist rotation
Progress from tuck to full lever
setup: Hang from rings, invert, then lower the body to a horizontal position facing the floor with arms straight.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips instead of staying rigid
Bending the arms to compensate for strength
Progressing to full lever before tuck mastery

formCues: Keep rings close to the body
Lower until upper arms are parallel to floor
Press up while controlling ring turnout
setup: Support your body above two gymnastic rings with arms straight and rings turned out slightly.
commonMistakes: Letting rings flare uncontrolled
Descending too fast without shoulder control
Not reaching adequate depth

formCues: Progress through tuck and advanced tuck first
setup: Hang from rings with straight arms, then pull the body to horizontal facing upward.
commonMistakes: Letting hips drop below shoulder line
Bending elbows to cheat the hold
Skipping progression stages too early

formCues: Press rings down and out slightly
setup: Grip two rings set at a stable height and kick up into an inverted handstand position.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back excessively
Letting rings drift and destabilize
Bent arms instead of full lockout

formCues: Lower head toward hand level with control
Press back up through the rings
setup: Kick up into a ring handstand with rings stabilized and body aligned overhead.
commonMistakes: Losing ring stability mid-rep
Flaring elbows during the press
Insufficient shoulder strength causing collapse

formCues: Keep body in a straight line
setup: Set rings at mid-height, lie underneath, and grip them with arms extended and body straight.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips during the pull
Not achieving full chest contact with rings
Using momentum instead of controlled pulling

formCues: Press rings down to support body
Lift legs straight out in front
setup: Support your body above the rings with arms straight, then raise both legs parallel to the floor.
commonMistakes: Shrugging shoulders instead of depressing them
Bending the knees to compensate
Rounding the lower back

formCues: Pull explosively while leaning slightly back
Transition rings around the wrists at the top of the pull
Press out over the rings to full lockout
Keep rings close to the body throughout
setup: Hang from rings with a false grip and arms fully extended.
commonMistakes: Kipping excessively instead of controlled strength
Failing to transition the grip cleanly
Pressing out with poor ring control

formCues: Keep rings stable, avoid excessive swing
Squeeze shoulder blades at the top
setup: Grip two rings with arms fully extended and body hanging freely.
commonMistakes: Excessive kipping or swinging
Not achieving full range of motion
Letting rings drift apart uncontrolled

setup: Set rings low near the floor, grip them, and assume a plank position with rings under the shoulders.
commonMistakes: Letting rings wobble uncontrolled
Sagging hips out of plank alignment
Cutting range of motion short

formCues: Tuck knees and rotate through slowly
Control the descent into an inverted hang
Reverse the motion back to start
setup: Hang from rings with straight arms and shoulders engaged before beginning the rotation.
commonMistakes: Rotating too fast without shoulder control
Skipping the tuck progression
Overextending the shoulders past comfortable range

formCues: Press rings down to full arm lockout
setup: Support your body above two rings with arms fully extended and locked out.
commonMistakes: Shrugging shoulders up toward ears
Letting rings drift and destabilize
Bent arms instead of full lockout

formCues: Brace core as hard as possible
Keep body in a rigid straight line
setup: Start in a forearm plank position with elbows under shoulders and body straight.
commonMistakes: Not generating full-body tension
Letting hips sag or pike up
Holding breath instead of controlled breathing

formCues: Keep pedal strokes smooth and circular
Shift gears to maintain steady cadence
setup: Mount the road bike with saddle height set so the knee has a slight bend at full pedal extension.
commonMistakes: Saddle set too low, causing knee strain
Death-gripping the handlebars
Mashing pedals instead of smooth circles

formCues: Swing arms forward and back, not across body
setup: Stand tall in running shoes on the road surface, ready to begin at an easy pace.
commonMistakes: Overstriding with heel-first landing
Slouching or leaning too far forward
Tensing shoulders and clenching fists
